prompt.context: Our client is a mid-size amusement park chain, with 10 parks around the U.S. serving over 10 million visitors each year. In their Richmond, VA park, it operates both a traditional thrill-ride section, as well as an animal experience. Currently, the two sections are covered under one entry ticket price. However, management is considering offering a separate ticket for only the animal experience section.
prompt.question: They have come to us to determine if this is a good idea. Should Seven Flags offer a separate animal-only admission ticket, and if so, at what price?

clarifying_info.q: What is the financial goal or success metric for this project?
clarifying_info.a: Management wants a payback period of less than 10 years. Payback period = investment / on-going profit.

clarifying_info.q: What is the current ticket price?
clarifying_info.a: Tickets are currently $20 and provide visitors full access to the park.

clarifying_info.q: How many visitors does the Richmond park see?
clarifying_info.a: The Richmond, VA park is an average sized park within the client's portfolio.

clarifying_info.q: How does the business model work?
clarifying_info.a: The park is a typical amusement park (think Six Flags or Busch Gardens). Visitors buy a ticket for entrance — same price for adults and children — and all rides and amusements are accessible under the one ticket price. The park also sells merchandise and food/drinks separately.

exhibits.title: Seven Flags Park Map
exhibits.shows: A map of the Seven Flags Richmond, VA park showing two distinct sections: the traditional thrill-ride section and the animal experience section, with their relative layout and entrances.
exhibits.data: Two park sections visible; current single-entry layout

framework: Incremental profit analysis: revenue impact (new animal-only ticket pricing, cannibalization of full-access ticket sales, food/drink/merchandise uplift) and cost impact (existing operating costs, new fixed capital costs)
Competitive landscape: other local attractions (zoos, petting zoos, museums, movie theaters, state fairs, family recreational activities)
Macro trends: changes in disposable income, weather conditions, consumer entertainment preferences

questions.prompt: From Exhibit 2 (price elasticity of animal-only admissions), which ticket price maximizes incremental revenue? Walk through your analysis.
questions.guidance: Candidate should build a table testing each price point ($10, $12, $14, $16), applying the 50% cannibalization rate and 350 operating days. Revenue is maximized at $16/ticket (~$1.05M incremental annual ticket revenue, ~5% increase over current $20M). Strong candidates note that results are highly sensitive to the cannibalization rate assumption.

math.setup: Current annual ticket revenue = ~1M visitors/yr x $20 = $20M. For each price point: New tickets sold (daily) = Total visitors x (1 - cannibalization rate). Cannibalized tickets (daily) = Total visitors x cannibalization rate. Daily incremental revenue = (price x new tickets) + ((price - $20) x cannibalized tickets). Annual incremental revenue = daily incremental revenue x 350 days.
steps: $10 price: 1,300 visitors/day; new tickets = 650; cannibalized = 650; daily incremental = $6,500 + (-$10 x 650) = $6,500 - $6,500 = $0; annual = $0
$12 price: 1,100 visitors/day; new tickets = 550; cannibalized = 550; daily incremental = $6,600 + (-$8 x 550) = $6,600 - $4,400 = $2,200; annual = $770,000
$14 price: 700 visitors/day; new tickets = 350; cannibalized = 350; daily incremental = $4,900 + (-$6 x 350) = $4,900 - $2,100 = $2,800; annual = $980,000
$16 price: 500 visitors/day; new tickets = 250; cannibalized = 250; daily incremental = $4,000 + (-$4 x 250) = $4,000 - $1,000 = $3,000; annual = $1,050,000
math.answer: $16 per ticket maximizes incremental annual revenue at $1,050,000, representing approximately a 5% increase over current $20M ticket revenue.

questions.prompt: What is the payback period for this investment, and does it meet management's requirement?
questions.guidance: Candidate should recognize the need to calculate payback period (ideally surfacing this from the clarifying info gathered at the start). Fixed cost investment is $2M (provided only if asked). Profit margin is 20%. Payback = $2M / ($1,050,000 x 20%) = ~9.5 years, just below the 10-year threshold. Strong candidates flag this is tight and sensitive to assumptions.

math.setup: Payback period = Investment / Incremental annual profit. Incremental annual profit = Incremental revenue x profit margin. Fixed investment = $2,000,000. Profit margin = 20%.
math.answer: ~9.5 years, which just meets management's requirement of less than 10 years.

brainstorming.prompt: Aside from ticket sales, what are some other considerations that will factor into the decision?

categories.name: Other revenue sources
ideas: Food and beverage sales to animal-section-only visitors
Parking fees from new visitors who would not have visited otherwise
Annual pass products (individual and family passes for animal section)

categories.name: Incremental costs
ideas: Build-out of new entrance for animal section
Construction of a wall or barrier to separate the rides section from the animal enclosure
Additional employees to staff the new entrance and handle higher visitor volume

recommendation: Move forward with creating an animal-only admission ticket priced at $16
At $16, incremental ticket revenue is maximized at ~$1,050,000 per year, representing a ~5% increase in total ticket revenues and profits
The $2M investment yields a payback period of ~9.5 years, just below management's 10-year requirement
risks: Incremental revenue and profit are highly sensitive to the cannibalization rate assumption — if actual cannibalization exceeds 50%, incremental profits will fall and the payback period will exceed 10 years
Potential opportunity cost: the $2M capital could be deployed in higher-ROI projects elsewhere in the portfolio
next_steps: Quantify the incremental food, beverage, and merchandise revenue from new animal-section-only visitors to size the upside opportunity and determine how much it could shorten the payback period
Validate the cannibalization rate assumption through customer surveys or test pricing before full rollout
